Model a solid circular shaft under linear-elastic, small-deformation torsion in the N-mm-MPa unit system throughout.
The shaft has length L = 1200 mm, diameter d = 30 mm, and is made of AISI 1020 steel with shear modulus G = 76923.1 MPa.
The shaft is cantilevered: fixed (zero rotation) at x = 0, free at x = L = 1200 mm, with no intermediate supports.
Two discrete torques are applied: T1 = +200000 N·mm at x = 1200 mm (free end, positive sense about the x-axis), and T2 = -200000 N·mm at x = 400 mm (negative sense about the x-axis).
Compute the fixed-end reaction torque from global equilibrium: T_reaction = -(T1 + T2).
Divide the shaft into two segments: Segment 1 from x = 0 to x = 400 mm, and Segment 2 from x = 400 mm to x = 1200 mm.
Compute the internal torque in each segment using the convention that internal torque equals the algebraic sum of all external torques applied to the portion of the shaft to the right of the cut section.
State the governing relation for internal torque: T_int(x) equals the sum of external torques on the right-hand free-body portion beyond the cut.
Compute the polar moment of inertia J = π d^4 / 32 and state its numerical value in mm^4.
Compute the torsional shear stress distribution in each segment using τ(r) = T_int · r / J, where r ranges from 0 to d/2, and report the maximum shear stress τ_max = T_int · (d/2) / J for each segment.
Compute the angle of twist per unit length in each segment using dφ/dx = T_int / (G J).
Integrate the twist rate from the fixed end using the boundary condition φ(0) = 0 to obtain φ(x) piecewise for both segments, ensuring continuity of φ at x = 400 mm.
Report the total angle of twist at the free end φ(L) in radians and convert it to degrees.
Present all results step by step in order: reaction, internal torque diagram values, J, shear stresses per segment, twist rate per segment, and piecewise twist angle expressions with the final numerical value at x = L.
Maintain full numerical precision during intermediate steps and round only in the final reported values to four significant figures.
